messages.text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?
I don’t have a price in mind. I want an independent valuation and my fair share based on that—I won’t subsidize A’s purchase. I’d like this settled fairly, but there’s no rush.

Thank you. My husband and I would like to buy the house, but I can’t give a price yet—we haven’t agreed one. We’d hope for a family discount, though I know C hasn’t agreed. What matters most to me is being able to build financial independence for us.

Thank you. I would like some money from the estate to start a dance studio; that matters most to me. I’m not sure what amount or shares would be fair, and I don’t want to presume. I hope we can work that out without pressuring anyone about the house.
Yes, I’d agree to an independent valuation. I’m not sure what the will says about each share or who the executor is; we should check the will.
Yes, an independent valuation seems a sensible first step. I’m not sure it would make each share clear by itself, though. I don’t know what the will says about the shares or who the executor is.
I’m not sure what the will says or who the executor is. We should check the will rather than assume.
That seems like a reasonable starting point, but I can’t agree to the price or shares until we’ve checked the will and valuation. I don’t know who has a copy of the will.
That seems like a reasonable way to proceed, as long as nobody is pressured and the will is checked before deciding shares. I don’t know who has a copy of it.
It works as a starting point, as long as any discount needs my agreement. I don’t know who has the will; we’ll need to ask around.
I’ll check his papers and ask whether his lawyer or bank has a copy.
That sounds sensible. I can look through Dad’s papers, and we can ask his lawyer or bank if needed.
Agreed. Let’s check his papers and contact his lawyer or bank; I’m happy to help look. No need to rush or assume anything until we find the will.
That works for me. I’ll contact his lawyer and bank, then share what I find with B and C.
That works for me. C and I can go through Dad’s papers and share anything we find with A.
That works. B and I will check his papers and share anything we find with you both.
